name: Conor Sheridan

education.notes: Listed on LinkedIn; exact years not pinned down from public sources. Worked in restaurants during school and university.

education.degree: MSc Economics and Strategy for Business
education.notes: Postgraduate degree that bridged him from undergraduate economics into finance/consulting.
Short executive program rather than a degree.

careerSteps.role: Strategic consultant, then quantitative trader / investment strategist / fund manager
keyDecisions: Started in strategic consulting, then moved into quantitative finance / automated fund management for Irish asset managers

Researched franchise opportunities from the trading desk for years, dreaming of getting into restaurants — never let go of the hospitality itch he developed working in restaurants through school and university
lessons: Quant finance trains pattern-recognition and data discipline that transfer to operating data-heavy businesses
A 'side passion' that survives a full finance career is a signal — not noise
careerSteps.notes: Pre-founder career in Irish financial services (incl. fund manager role at Davy). Built capital, network and analytical rigour before stepping into hospitality.

keyDecisions: Chose to build a new concept rather than buy a franchise: 'Instead of opening a franchise like Subway, which would've been the normal decision, I decided to build something new. It came down to control — creative and entrepreneurial control.'
Launched Ireland's first dedicated fried-chicken-sandwich restaurant on Camden Street, Dublin in 2018
Scaled to a second location within four months, third within eleven months — ~€5M revenue and 90 staff inside year one
Stayed on as director while building Nory in parallel
lessons: Operating a real-world business in person is the cheapest way to discover the actual pain points of an industry
Painful, manual back-office work in hospitality (rostering, stock, forecasting) is the wedge that became Nory
Surviving COVID via takeaway/delivery taught operational resilience that no consultant could simulate
careerSteps.notes: Mad Egg's PMF was almost immediate; the operational complexity of scaling it directly inspired Nory.

keyDecisions: Began by building internal algorithms for Mad Egg's demand prediction, staffing and ordering
Applied to Dogpatch Labs during the pandemic and hired the founding team

Initially integrated via APIs with incumbent restaurant tools — then chose to own the full operating system: 'These incumbents could block us strategically… To scale, we needed to own the workflows, the data gravity, and the account gravity.'
Bootstrapped initially, then raised £1.5M pre-seed (2021, Playfair + Cavalry Ventures), $16M Series A (May 2024, led by Accel) and $37M Series B (Sep 2025, led by Kinnevik)
Expanded into US, Europe and Middle East serving ~300 hospitality clients
lessons: Operator-founders building tools they wished they had during a prior business have unique product insight
Vertical AI for legacy industries (hospitality) is a wide-open European playing field where US-tooling is weak
Solo founder + Series B is achievable in Europe when the customer credibility comes from your own operating business
'Bootstrap your first startup to appreciate profitability' — finance background + hands-on Mad Egg P&L instilled this
careerSteps.notes: Total raised ≈ $62.6M. Reported ~$5M ARR at Series B. Customers across US, Europe, Middle East including restaurants associated with Jamie Oliver, Chopped, Viva Italia.

outcomes.currentStatus: Founder & CEO of Nory (AI-native restaurant OS, ~300 clients globally, ~$5M ARR, ~$62.6M raised). Still director of Mad Egg.

lessons.lesson: Operator-founders who build tools for an industry they have personally run carry rare product instinct.
European vertical AI is under-served — Irish/UK founders can win categories US incumbents ignore.
Bootstrap your first startup to appreciate profitability — the discipline carries into the VC-backed second.
Own the workflows, data gravity and account gravity — integration-only plays are strategically blockable by incumbents.

notes: AI-revolution era Irish vertical-SaaS founder. Unusually clean operator → hustler → founder arc: finance (Davy/FAT/YPO) → real-world restaurant operator (Mad Egg) → AI-for-restaurants (Nory). European context: Dublin-based, raised from US (Accel) and European (Kinnevik) tier-1 investors without relocating, demonstrating that you can build a globally-relevant vertical-AI company from Ireland.
